job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his father were driving to the local market on a sunny Sunday morning. As they approached a busy intersection, the traffic light turned amber. Rohan’s father immediately slowed down to a halt, explaining that amber means prepare to stop, not speed up. Rohan noticed a circular road sign nearby and asked if it was just a suggestion. His father clarified that road signs are mandatory rules, not mere advice. As they drove, Rohan noticed a man on a scooter without a helmet, claiming it was just a short ride to the shop. His father shook his head, noting that safety gear is essential regardless of distance. They soon passed a pedestrian crossing where a group of children waited patiently for the cars to stop before stepping onto the road. Rohan’s father reminded him that even at a crossing, one must always look both ways before walking. Finally, as they reached the market, Rohan’s father buckled his seatbelt and reminded Rohan to do the same, even though they were driving slowly. He explained that seatbelts are vital at any speed to prevent injury during sudden stops. Rohan realized that traffic rules exist to protect everyone, and following them is a responsibility for every driver and passenger, regardless of the distance or the speed of the vehicle.
response.summary: This story highlights the importance of following traffic rules like obeying signals and wearing safety gear. It emphasizes that safety measures are mandatory for everyone, regardless of speed or distance traveled.
